name: General Aptitude
description: The 15 marks every GATE paper shares: verbal ability, quantitative aptitude, analytical reasoning and spatial thinking.

nodes.name: Grammar and usage
nodes.desc: Articles, prepositions, tenses, subject–verb agreement and the error-spotting questions built on them.
nodes.summary: You will be able to spot and fix the grammar errors GATE sets in sentence-completion and error-spotting questions.

nodes.name: Vocabulary
nodes.desc: Synonyms, antonyms, word pairs and analogies, and choosing the word that fits the context.
nodes.summary: You will be able to choose the right word from context and solve synonym, antonym and analogy questions quickly.

nodes.name: Reading comprehension
nodes.desc: Reading a short passage for its main idea, inferences and the statement that follows from it.
nodes.summary: You will be able to read a short passage and pick the inference, main idea or assumption that it actually supports.

nodes.name: Numbers and arithmetic
nodes.desc: Divisibility, remainders, HCF and LCM, fractions and the arithmetic shortcuts aptitude questions rely on.
nodes.summary: You will be able to handle divisibility, remainders, HCF, LCM and fraction arithmetic quickly and without a calculator.

nodes.name: Percentages, ratio and proportion
nodes.desc: Percent change, profit and loss, ratios, mixtures and proportional reasoning.
nodes.summary: You will be able to solve percentage, profit and loss, ratio and mixture problems with clean proportional reasoning.

nodes.name: Time, work and speed
nodes.desc: Work rates, pipes and cisterns, speed, distance and relative motion.
nodes.summary: You will be able to set up rate equations for work, pipes, speed and relative motion problems and solve them fast.

nodes.name: Data interpretation
nodes.desc: Reading tables, bar and pie charts, and computing the percentages and ratios they ask for.
nodes.summary: You will be able to read tables and charts accurately and compute the percentages, ratios and trends a question asks for.

nodes.name: Counting and chance
nodes.desc: Permutations, combinations and simple probability as GATE aptitude asks them.
nodes.summary: You will be able to count arrangements and selections and compute simple probabilities in aptitude-style questions.

nodes.name: Logical reasoning
nodes.desc: Statements and conclusions, syllogisms, and deciding what must, could or cannot be true.
nodes.summary: You will be able to decide which conclusions follow from given statements, including syllogisms and must-be-true questions.
topics: Must, could and cannot be true

nodes.name: Arrangements and puzzles
nodes.desc: Seating arrangements, ordering, blood relations and the grid puzzles that test careful casework.
nodes.summary: You will be able to solve seating, ordering and relation puzzles by laying out the constraints and eliminating cases.

nodes.name: Series and patterns
nodes.desc: Number and letter series, coding–decoding and spotting the rule behind a sequence.
nodes.summary: You will be able to find the rule behind number and letter series and decode coded words reliably.

nodes.name: Spatial reasoning
nodes.desc: Paper folding, mirror images, rotations, cubes and counting figures.
nodes.summary: You will be able to reason about folds, mirror images, rotations and cubes to answer spatial questions without drawing everything.

nodes.name: Geometry and mensuration
nodes.desc: Areas, perimeters and volumes of common shapes, and the geometry facts aptitude questions use.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute areas, perimeters and volumes of common shapes and use basic geometry facts in aptitude questions.
